correctness.rationale: For d=2k, parity of k coordinates yields k neighbors of each color, while one color is excluded by positive degree. Two colors cannot meet the floor-half cap in odd degree. In Q3 every pair on the same parity side shares a neighbor, so that side needs four colors. In Q5 a hypothetical three-coloring forces multiplicities (2,2,1) at each vertex. On one parity side a color class of size s then has 5s=16+t where t even-side neighborhoods have two members; every distance-two pair contributes two such incidences and distance-four pairs contribute none, hence t=2e_2 and s is 4 or 6. For six members, exactly eight pairs would be at distance four. This induced graph is triangle-free with codegrees at most two, since the distance-four generators are the all-ones vector with one coordinate removed, and sums of two different generators are distance-two vectors with two ordered representations. On six vertices a triangle-free nonbipartite graph has a chordless five-cycle and at most two further edges; the bipartite splits with capacity for eight edges are 2:4 and 3:3, both requiring codegree at least three. Thus all three classes would have size four, not totaling sixteen. A separate exhaustive local-incidence check (`python3 /workspace/branches/independent_checks.py 2`) found 40 admissible individual classes, all of size four, among the 65,536 subsets of the odd half of Q5. Two-bit syndrome maps realize four colors for d=3,5; seven distinct nonzero three-bit changes realize the claimed 3,3,2 construction on Q7 (also checked with a different partition). In the two-coordinate lift, flipping the first new coordinate preserves the color and flipping the second changes it; at most one neighbor of any color is added, which exactly matches the increased cap. This proves the classification for all integers d>=2, not just the finite checks. The frozen checker uses int.bit_count(), requiring Python 3.10+, despite the 3.8+ reproducibility note; this does not affect the theorem.

broader_coverage.reasoning: A Q5 is not a complete multipartite graph (it is connected and bipartite, but not complete bipartite), and a perfect-coloring census does not cover arbitrary local frequency caps. The general bounds do not settle the exact values claimed across dimensions.

evidence: A (3,3,2) multifold Hamming-code partition gives precisely those cell sizes in every closed neighborhood. Theorem 3 requires perfect coloring and correlation immunity.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Deleting the center only reduces the closed-neighborhood multiplicities, so the Q7 existence statement follows directly and is not original. At Q5 the open count bound does not require equitable transition counts or correlation immunity, so the restricted census does not exclude a hypothetical nonperfect coloring; the six-vertex obstruction does. The full result also proves the all-odd lift.

value.rationale: This gives the exact invariant for a canonical infinite graph family. In dimension five the need for a fourth color persists even without any symmetry or equitability assumption; the link to the extremal six-vertex distance-four subgraph explains why, rather than just providing a solver count. The parity and lifting constructions identify the stable regime, incorporating rather than reinventing the known Q7 existence result.
